result.topic_en: Euler introduces angles φ and ψ to reduce the differential equation to dφ + r dψ = 0, then determines constants α, β, γ so that tan φ = αu + β, finding γγ = mm + nn + 1.

34. Evidens autem est integrationem utriusque partis, omissa scilicet littera $r$, ad certum arcum circularem reduci. Hanc ob rem hos ipsos angulos in calculum introducamus, ponendo: $\frac{\gamma\partial u}{1+uu+(mu+n)^2}=\partial\Phi$ et
$\frac{\gamma\partial p}{1+pp+(mp+n)^2}=\partial\psi$.
Sicque aequatio nostra ad hanc formam simplicissimam reducetur: $\partial\Phi+r\partial\psi=0$. Totum igitur negotium huc redit, quemadmodum hanc aequationem tractari atque ad integrabilitatem reduci oporteat. Evidens autem est hanc aequationem differentialia secundi gradus involvere.
35. Facile quidem patet angulum $\Phi$ ita esse comparatum, ut ejus tangens tali forma: $\alpha u+\beta$ exprimatur; quare si statuamus tg. $\Phi=\alpha u+\beta$, erit $\partial\Phi=\frac{\alpha\partial u}{1+(\alpha u+\beta)^2}$. Haec jam forma cum proposita comparetur, ut inde valores litterarum $\alpha$ et $\beta$, una cum $\gamma$, per litteras $m$ et $n$ determinentur, id quod fiet hanc aequationem:
$\alpha(1+uu+(mu+n)^2)=\gamma(1+(\alpha u+\beta)^2)$,
identicam reddendo. Hunc in finem cum facta evolutione sequens oriatur aequatio:
$\alpha(mm+1)uu+2\alpha mnu+\alpha(nn+1)=\alpha\alpha\gamma uu+2\gamma\alpha\beta u+\gamma(\beta\beta+1)$,
inde tres sequentes elicimus determinationes:
1°. $\alpha\gamma=mm+1$; 2°. $\beta\gamma=mn$; 3°. $\gamma(\beta\beta+1)=\alpha(nn+1)$;
ex quarum prima colligitur $\alpha=\frac{mm+1}{\gamma}$; ex secunda $\beta=\frac{mn}{\gamma}$,
qui valores in tertia substituti dant $\gamma\gamma=mm+nn+1$,

items.quote: Evidens autem est integrationem utriusque partis, omissa scilicet littera $r$, ad certum arcum circularem reduci.
items.english: It is evident that the integration of each part, omitting the letter r, reduces to a certain circular arc.

items.quote: Totum igitur negotium huc redit, quemadmodum hanc aequationem tractari atque ad integrabilitatem reduci oporteat.
items.english: The whole business therefore comes down to how this equation should be treated and reduced to integrability.

items.quote: Evidens autem est hanc aequationem differentialia secundi gradus involvere.
items.english: It is evident that this equation involves differentials of the second degree.

items.english: It is easily seen that the angle Φ is such that its tangent is expressed in the form αu + β.
